# What does multimodal alignment align: vectors, visual interfaces, or evidence dependence?

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-07 · 21 topic entries / 7 representative comparisons

CLIP and EmbeddingGemma 2 produce comparable vectors. BLIP-2 and LLaVA connect vision to conditional generation, CV-OPD trains visual evidence use, and UMRM scores responses. Their supervision and interfaces differ, not a single capability ladder.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### A shared retrieval space is not a language input space

CLIP and EmbeddingGemma 2 align vector similarities; the latter supports selected MRL dimensions. BLIP-2 queries and LLaVA projections condition an LLM and require generative training to use them. Matching dimensions or retrieval semantics do not make a vector a general-purpose visual soft prompt.

Sources: [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md) · [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md) · [BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en.md) · [Visual Instruction Tuning](../../../../reproductions/2304.08485-llava/README-en.md)

### A good-looking answer and genuine image evidence use differ

UMRM learns rewards from caption perturbations and checks selection of policy-generated responses, rather than only hand-built negatives. CV-OPD changes teacher crops under a fixed student prefix to constrain distributions directly. Evaluation and distillation can complement each other without a reward benchmark proving visual attribution.

Sources: [Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling](../../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en.md) · [CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation](../../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en.md) · [Visual Instruction Tuning](../../../../reproductions/2304.08485-llava/README-en.md)

### October 29: publication update and evidence boundary

The formal EmbeddingGemma 2 paper is the October 6 model, not a new identity. It describes pooling 512-dimensional backbone features then projecting to 768. Pinned official code projects before returning `last_hidden_state`; equal-weight masked means commute with that linear map. Keep the 16-image GPU result at its prior evidence grade, not audio/video or seven-benchmark acceptance.

Sources: [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md) · [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md)

### Speech embeddings, discrete speech units, and translation candidates are different output interfaces

EmbeddingGemma 2 maps multiple modalities to comparable fixed-width vectors, with MRL reducing vector width. GSLM2 extracts several time-aligned discrete streams from the same speech, so joint deduplication changes sequence length; its stream-specific heads score spoken candidates conditioned on shared history. NaijaS2ST instead requires cross-language speech generation and evaluates it with translation references and ASR-COMET. Vector neighbors, same-language paired discrimination and cross-language generation cannot share one accuracy measure. The local GSLM2 slice verifies transformations of supplied units and probabilities, not real speech capability.

Sources: [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md) · [GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.01143-gslm2/README-en.md) · [NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages](../../../../multimodal-models/2604.16287-naijas2st/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why doesn't correct image retrieval with CLIP or EmbeddingGemma 2 show LLaVA can answer image questions? {#cross-embedding-versus-answer}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Retrieval matches candidate representations. LLaVA generates answer tokens from an image, question, and context, which needs a generative interface and supervision. Compare the same output task, not retrieval hits pooled with answer correctness.

    **Illustrative example:** Retrieving an image of cups does not establish counting them, citing evidence, or following an answer format.

    Sources: [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md) · [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md) · [Visual Instruction Tuning](../../../../reproductions/2304.08485-llava/README-en.md)

### Do fewer BLIP-2 queries and narrower EmbeddingGemma 2 vectors save the same resource? {#cross-two-compression-axes}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Q-Former queries determine visual sequence length to the LLM. MRL width affects retrieval-vector storage and similarity. Both can lose information but at different stages; use trained prefixes with renormalization, not coordinate deletion as visual pooling.

    **Illustrative example:** Thirty-two visual tokens and a 256-dimensional vector are length and width, not directly comparable.

    Sources: [BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en.md) · [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md)

### Does UMRM detecting a caption color perturbation show the CV-OPD student uses the right image region? {#cross-reward-versus-visual-dependence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** UMRM ranks one negative distribution, while policy errors can differ. CV-OPD compares student and positive/negative crop teachers on a shared prefix. Correct judging, receiving that training signal, and genuinely changing evidence use are separate checks.

    **Illustrative example:** A judge spotting red changed to blue does not show the student stopped guessing common colors.

    Sources: [Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling](../../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en.md) · [CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation](../../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en.md)

### When can prior results survive a difference between paper and code operator order? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Check the actual operations. The same bias-free linear projection commutes with equal-weight masked averaging and the pinned code/checkpoint did not change. Nonlinearity, different weights, or retraining do not inherit equivalence. Only provenance changes here.

    **Illustrative example:** `mean(W h1,W h2)=W mean(h1,h2)`; averaging two GELU outputs generally does not equal GELU of their mean.

    Sources: [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md) · [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md)

### To compare which spoken continuation is more plausible, can a unified audio embedding similarity replace GSLM2's transition score? {#cross-nov07-speech-stream-versus-embedding}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** They are not equivalent. EmbeddingGemma 2's fixed vector supports object similarity. GSLM2's score uses sequential conditional probabilities at first and changed positions per stream, then weights streams equally. Continuations can match the same topic while differing in grammar or phonetic transitions. Translation needs a separate cross-language protocol such as NaijaS2ST.

    **Illustrative example:** Example: Two endings mention a cup and may be close in embedding space, but only one uses the right verb form in context. Compare sequence scores and retrieval similarity separately; do not report the latter as sBLIMP accuracy.

    Sources: [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md) · [GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.01143-gslm2/README-en.md) · [NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages](../../../../multimodal-models/2604.16287-naijas2st/README-en.md)
